literal: Comparing ancient to present, the omen is one."
idiomatic: The omen is the same."

literal: By the seventh month he indeed was defeated.
idiomatic: By the seventh month he was indeed defeated.

literal: Early in Xiaowu he was posthumously given Grand Preceptor and Grand Marshal.
idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was posthumously made grand preceptor and grand marshal.

literal: Hao's younger brother Xuan, at the start of Emperor Zhuang, was enfeoffed Prince of Donghai and made Director of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: Hao's younger brother Xuan, at the start of Emperor Zhuang's reign, was enfeoffed Prince of Donghai and made director of the secretariat.

literal: When Hao entered Luoyang and success or failure was not yet divided, he was self-satisfied from spirit; men of the time laughed.
idiomatic: When Hao entered Luoyang and the outcome was still in doubt, Xuan swaggered with self-satisfaction; men of the time laughed.

literal: When Hao was defeated he hid in secret flight; a man seized and delivered him; he was beheaded in the market.
idiomatic: When Hao fell he fled in hiding; a man seized him and delivered him; he was beheaded in the market.

literal: Early in Xiaowu he was posthumously given Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was posthumously made grand commandant.

literal: Xiaowen's seven sons: after Deposed Empress Lin, Deposed Crown Prince Xun;
idiomatic: Xiaowen had seven sons: by Deposed Empress Lin, Deposed Crown Prince Xun;

literal: by Empress Wen Zhao, Emperor Xuandi and Prince of Guangping Wu Mu Huai;
idiomatic: by Empress Wen Zhao, Emperor Xuandi and Prince of Guangping Wu Mu Huai;

literal: by Lady Yuan, Prince of Jingzhao Yu;
idiomatic: by Lady Yuan, Prince of Jingzhao Yu;

literal: by Lady Luo, Prince of Qinghe Wen Xian Yi and Prince of Runan Yue;
idiomatic: by Lady Luo, Prince of Qinghe Wen Xian Yi and Prince of Runan Yue;

literal: by Lady Zheng Chonghua, the prince Tiao, not enfeoffed, died early.
idiomatic: by Lady Zheng Chonghua, the prince Tiao, who was never enfeoffed and died young.

literal: Deposed Crown Prince the commoner Xun, styled Yuandao.
idiomatic: Deposed Crown Prince, the commoner Xun, styled Yuandao.

literal: At birth his mother died; Empress Dowager Wenming nursed and watched him, often keeping him at her side.
idiomatic: His mother died at his birth; Empress Dowager Wenming nursed him and kept him always at her side.

literal: At four years the empress dowager personally established his name Xun, styled Yuandao.
idiomatic: At four the empress dowager herself gave him the name Xun and the style Yuandao.

literal: Thereupon there was a great amnesty.
idiomatic: Thereupon the court proclaimed a great amnesty.

literal: In the seventh month, day guichou, of the seventeenth year of Taihe, Xun was established as crown prince.
idiomatic: On guichou of the seventh month, Taihe 17, Xun was established as crown prince.

literal: At the capping in the temple, Xiaowen at the eastern hall of Guangji summoned Xun in to see him and admonished him on the capping rite, saying: "I style you Yuandao; what is entrusted is not light—you should seek the meaning in the name and follow my intent."
idiomatic: At his capping in the temple Xiaowen received him at the eastern hall of Guangji and taught him the rite: "I style you Yuandao; what is entrusted is not light. Seek the meaning in the name and follow my intent."

literal: In the twentieth year his style was changed to Xuandao.
idiomatic: In the twentieth year his style was changed to Xuandao.

literal: When the capital moved to Luoyang, an edict sent Xun to the capital at Dai; his comings and goings, ritual and bearing, the emperor all fixed.
idiomatic: When the capital moved to Luoyang, an edict sent Xun to the old capital at Dai; the emperor fixed every detail of his journey, ritual, and bearing.

literal: When Xun entered to take leave, the emperor said: "Now you ought not go toward Dai.
idiomatic: When Xun came to take leave the emperor said, "You ought not go to Dai now.

literal: But the Grand Preceptor died at Heng; I already bear the heavy weight of the imperial apex and cannot lightly go to my maternal uncle's mourning; I wish you to show mourning for your uncle, bow at your mother's tomb, and write out once the feeling of a son.
idiomatic: The Grand Preceptor died at Heng. I bear the weight of the throne and cannot lightly attend my uncle's mourning. Go show mourning for your uncle, bow at your mother's tomb, and once write out a son's feeling.

literal: At the northern hills and tombs, when you arrive there, after the Grand Preceptor's affairs are finished, on another day you should once bow at the hills and tombs.
idiomatic: At the northern hills and tombs, when the Grand Preceptor's rites are finished, on another day bow once at the tombs.

literal: When the bowing is done, your clan ancestor Prince of Nan'an may be visited once for inquiry.
idiomatic: When that is done, you may once visit your clan ancestor Prince of Nan'an.

literal: On the road you should warmly read the classics; today you see me in person."
idiomatic: On the road read the classics with care; today you see me face to face."

literal: Afterward each year when the emperor campaigned, Xun often remained to defend and presided over temple sacrifice.
idiomatic: Afterward, whenever the emperor campaigned, Xun often remained behind to guard the capital and preside over temple sacrifice.

literal: Xun did not love letters and learning; his body was large and fat; he deeply hated the heat of the Yellow and Luo rivers and in mind often yearned for the pleasures of the north.
idiomatic: Xun did not love books; he was large and heavy of body; he hated the heat of the Luo valley and longed in his heart for the north.

literal: Junior mentor Gao Daoyue repeatedly spoke in bitter remonstrance; Xun deeply resented him.
idiomatic: Junior mentor Gao Daoyue remonstrated again and again; Xun deeply resented him.

literal: When Xiaowen visited Song Mountain, Xun remained at Jincheng, plotting to summon the horse herds and with light cavalry flee to Dai, and with his own hand killed Daoyue in the forbidden precinct.
idiomatic: When Xiaowen visited Song Mountain, Xun remained at Jincheng, plotted to summon the horse herds and flee to Dai with light cavalry, and with his own hand killed Daoyue in the palace.

literal: Commander of the Palace Guard Yuan Hui restrained the gate guards and held them back; by night all was quiet.
idiomatic: Commander of the Palace Guard Yuan Hui held the gate guards back; by night all was quiet.

literal: When the emperor heard he was shocked and grieved; outwardly he concealed the affair and still went to Bian Ford and returned.
idiomatic: The emperor was shocked and grieved when he heard, but outwardly concealed the affair and still went to Bian Ford and returned.

literal: He summoned Xun and counted his crimes; with Prince of Xianyang Xi and others he personally beat Xun with staves.
idiomatic: He summoned Xun, counted his crimes, and with Prince of Xianyang Xi and others personally beat him with staves.

literal: He also had Xi and the others take turns for more than a hundred blows; they dragged him out; for more than a month he could not rise.
idiomatic: He had Xi and the others take turns for more than a hundred blows, then drag him out; for more than a month he could not rise.

literal: He was confined in a separate lodge west of the city.
idiomatic: He was confined in a separate lodge west of the city.

literal: He summoned the ministers to audience at Qingwei Hall to deliberate deposing him.
idiomatic: He summoned the ministers to Qingwei Hall to deliberate deposing him.

literal: Minister of Works and Crown Prince's Grand Tutor Mu Liang, Vice Minister of Works and Junior Guardian Li Chong, all removed caps and bowed to the ground in apology.
idiomatic: Minister of Works and the crown prince's grand tutor Mu Liang, and Vice Minister of Works and junior guardian Li Chong, all removed their caps and bowed to the ground in apology.

literal: The emperor said: "The ancients had a saying: great righteousness destroys kin.
idiomatic: The emperor said, "The ancients said that great righteousness destroys kin.

literal: If this boy is not destroyed today, it is the state's great calamity.
idiomatic: If this boy is not destroyed today, it will be the state's great calamity.

literal: If you wait until I have no heir, I fear there will be chaos like the Yongjia era."
idiomatic: If you wait until I have no heir, I fear chaos like the Yongjia era."

literal: He was deposed as commoner and placed at Heyang;
idiomatic: He was deposed to commoner status and placed at Heyang.

literal: food and clothing supplied were only enough roughly to escape hunger and cold.
idiomatic: Food and clothing were only enough roughly to escape hunger and cold.

literal: When the emperor went to Dai he then went as to Chang'an; Imperial Censor Li Biao seized an opening for a secret memorial, reporting that Xun again with his attendants plotted rebellion.
idiomatic: When the emperor went to Dai and then toward Chang'an, Imperial Censor Li Biao seized an opening for a secret memorial, reporting that Xun again plotted rebellion with his attendants.

literal: The emperor was at Chang'an; he sent Attendant of the Secretariat Xing Luan with Prince of Xianyang Xi, bearing an edict with peppered wine, to Heyang and granted Xun death.
idiomatic: The emperor was at Chang'an; he sent Attendant of the Secretariat Xing Luan with Prince of Xianyang Xi, bearing an edict with peppered wine, to Heyang to grant Xun death.

literal: At the time he was a little more than fifteen.
idiomatic: He was a little more than fifteen.

literal: He was encoffined in a coarse coffin in ordinary dress and buried in Heyang city.
idiomatic: He was buried in a coarse coffin in ordinary dress at Heyang.

literal: In the winter of the twenty-second year, Censorate clerk Long Wenguan sat for a crime that should die and reported to the Court of Justice that on the days when Xun was repeatedly taken by attendants left and right, there was a hand document of self-explanation whose circumstances he did not know.
idiomatic: In the winter of the twenty-second year, censorate clerk Long Wenguan faced death for a crime and reported to the Court of Justice that on the days when Xun was repeatedly taken by attendants, there had been a handwritten plea whose circumstances he did not know.

literal: But Imperial Censor Li Biao and Attending Censor Jia Shang suppressed it and did not report.
idiomatic: But Imperial Censor Li Biao and attending censor Jia Shang suppressed it and did not report.

literal: Jia sat in the Court of Justice for it.
idiomatic: Jia was imprisoned in the Court of Justice for it.

literal: At the time Biao was dismissed and returned home; the emperor was at Ye; the Ministry of Works memorialized to seize Biao and send him to Luoyang; an amnesty came and the root and branch were not pursued to the end.
idiomatic: At the time Biao had been dismissed and was home; the emperor was at Ye; the Ministry of Works memorialized to seize Biao and send him to Luoyang; an amnesty came and the matter was not pursued to the end.

literal: Jia Shang left imprisonment; he suddenly fell ill and died within several days.
idiomatic: Jia Shang left prison, fell suddenly ill, and died within days.

literal: At first the emperor was about to marry Xun to the eldest daughter of Minister of Works Feng Dan; because the girl was young he waited until she was older; first he betrothed as left and right Ruzi the daughters of Pengcheng Liu Changwen and Rongyang Zheng Yi.
idiomatic: At first the emperor meant to marry Xun to Minister of Works Feng Dan's eldest daughter; because the girl was young he waited; first he betrothed as left and right ruzi the daughters of Liu Changwen of Pengcheng and Zheng Yi of Rongyang.

literal: At the time Xun was thirteen or fourteen; the emperor once said to Guo Zuo, Cui Guang, and Song Bian: "A man's life must release himself; he cannot read books all morning.
idiomatic: When Xun was thirteen or fourteen the emperor once told Guo Zuo, Cui Guang, and Song Bian, "A man must sometimes release himself; he cannot read all morning.

literal: I wish Xun to go out in the morning to review the classics, return inside after eating, go out again at the hour of the monkey, and cease at dusk.
idiomatic: I want Xun to go out in the morning to study the classics, return after the meal, go out again at the monkey hour, and cease at dusk.

literal: What do you think?"
idiomatic: What do you think?"

literal: Guang said: "Confucius said that when blood and qi are not settled, one is on guard against lust.
idiomatic: Guang said, "Confucius warned that when blood and qi are unsettled, one must guard against lust.

literal: The crown prince is still in the years of first entering study; he ought not in the hours of full daylight leave books and enter the inner quarters; it is also not what secures a tender body and fixes the years of life."
idiomatic: The crown prince is still in his first years of study; he ought not in broad daylight leave his books for the inner quarters; that is no way to secure a tender body and fix the years of life."

literal: The emperor took Guang's words as right and then did not have Xun enter inside in daylight.
idiomatic: The emperor took Guang's words as right and would not let Xun enter the inner quarters by day.

literal: He had no sons.
idiomatic: He had no sons.

literal: Prince of Jingzhao Yu, styled Xuande, was enfeoffed in the twenty-first year of Taihe and made Commander-in-Chief and Governor of Xuzhou.
idiomatic: Prince of Jingzhao Yu, styled Xuande, was enfeoffed in Taihe 21 and made commander-in-chief and governor of Xuzhou.

literal: He made Prince of Pengcheng's Central Propaganda Office senior administrator Lu Yangwu concurrent senior administrator; all details of the province were entrusted to Yangwu.
idiomatic: He made Prince of Pengcheng's senior administrator of the Central Propaganda Office Lu Yangwu concurrent senior administrator; every detail of the province was entrusted to Yangwu.

literal: Early in Xuandi he was General Who Protects the Army.
idiomatic: Early in Xuandi's reign he was general who protects the army.

literal: The emperor kept his beloved younger brothers; Yu and the others often went in and out of the palace women's quarters, morning and evening lodging like family.
idiomatic: The emperor kept his beloved younger brothers near; Yu and the others often entered the palace women's quarters and lodged morning and evening like family.

literal: He was moved to Director of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: He was moved to director of the secretariat.

literal: He took as consort the younger sister of Empress Shun but did not answer her with ritual courtesy.
idiomatic: He took Empress Shun's younger sister as consort but never answered her with the courtesy owed a wife.

literal: Yu at Xuzhou took a concubine Lady Li, originally surnamed Yang of Dongjun; at night he heard her song, was pleased, and she came to be favored.
idiomatic: At Xuzhou Yu took a concubine, Lady Li, born Yang of Dongjun; hearing her sing at night he was pleased, and she won his favor.

literal: When he left the province and returned to the capital he wished to advance her to honored status.
idiomatic: When he left the province for the capital he wished to raise her to honored status.

literal: He entrusted Right Gentleman of the Palace Li Shixian of Zhao commandery to be her adoptive father and went through the rites to welcome her; she bore the son Baoyue.
idiomatic: He entrusted Right Gentleman of the Palace Li Shixian of Zhao to be her adoptive father, welcomed her by rite, and she bore the son Baoyue.

literal: Empress Shun summoned Li into the palace and beat and injured her.
idiomatic: Empress Shun summoned Li into the palace and beat her until she was injured.

literal: She was forced to become a nun inside; the son was given to the consort to rear.
idiomatic: She was forced to become a nun inside the palace; the son was given to the consort to rear.

literal: After more than a year the empress's father Yu Jin, because the empress long had borne no child, then memorialized urging broadening of the secondary harem.
idiomatic: After more than a year the empress's father Yu Jin, because the empress long bore no child, memorialized urging a broader harem.

literal: Thereupon he had the empress return Li to Yu; the old love was even greater.
idiomatic: Thereupon he had the empress return Li to Yu; the old love burned hotter.

literal: Yu loved letters and was quite accomplished in poetry and rhapsody.
idiomatic: Yu loved letters and was accomplished in poetry and rhapsody.

literal: At the time he often drew men of talent Song Shijing, Li Shenjun, Zu Ying, Xing Yan, Wang Zunye, Zhang Shiqi, and others to share feasts and joy.
idiomatic: He often drew men of talent—Song Shijing, Li Shenjun, Zu Ying, Xing Yan, Wang Zunye, Zhang Shiqi, and others—to share feasts and joy.

literal: He recruited several tens of Confucian guests from the four quarters such as Yan Huaiyan and lodged and honored them.
idiomatic: He recruited several tens of Confucian guests from the four quarters, such as Yan Huaiyan, lodged them, and honored them.

literal: The grain and cloth he received he mostly gave away in distribution.
idiomatic: The grain and cloth he received he mostly gave away.

literal: He also honored and believed in the Buddhist Way; expenses often reached the point of not meeting needs.
idiomatic: He also honored the Buddhist way; his expenses often outran his means.

literal: With his younger brother Prince of Guangping Huai he quite mutually boasted and admired, competing in extravagant splendor, greedy and lawless.
idiomatic: With his younger brother Prince of Guangping Huai he boasted and admired each other, competing in splendor, greedy and lawless.

literal: Thereupon Xuandi confined Yu in the palace to investigate, beat Yu fifty blows, and sent him out as Governor of Ji.
idiomatic: Thereupon Xuandi confined Yu in the palace to investigate, beat him fifty blows, and sent him out as governor of Ji.

literal: At first Yu himself thought that in office he sought attendance on important matters, his power weaker than his two younger brothers, and secretly harbored shame and resentment, often showing it in words and looks.
idiomatic: At first Yu had sought attendance on weighty affairs by office, found his power weaker than his two younger brothers, and secretly nursed shame and resentment, often showing it in word and face.

literal: Also because his favored concubine was repeatedly humiliated, inside and outside were estranged and suppressed.
idiomatic: Also because his favored concubine was repeatedly humiliated, he was estranged within and suppressed without.

literal: When he was in the province he plotted rebellion.
idiomatic: In the province he plotted rebellion.

literal: Yu then killed Senior Administrator Yang Lingyin and Marshal Li Zun, claiming to have received a secret document from Prince of Qinghe saying Gao Zhao plotted to kill the ruler.
idiomatic: Yu then killed Senior Administrator Yang Lingyin and Marshal Li Zun, claiming a secret document from Prince of Qinghe that Gao Zhao plotted to kill the ruler.

literal: He then made an altar south of Xindu, burned firewood and reported to Heaven, and at once took the imperial position.
idiomatic: He made an altar south of Xindu, burned firewood and reported to Heaven, and at once took the imperial position.

literal: He amnestied the realm, era name Jianping 1, and established Lady Li as empress.
idiomatic: He amnestied the realm, proclaimed the era Jianping 1, and made Lady Li empress.

literal: Xuandi ordered Minister of Works Li Ping to attack Yu.
idiomatic: Xuandi ordered Minister of Works Li Ping to attack Yu.

literal: Yu went out to resist the imperial army, was repeatedly defeated, and then surrounded the city and held it.
idiomatic: Yu went out to resist the imperial army, was repeatedly defeated, and then held the city under siege.

literal: Yu knew affairs were exhausted; he took Li and several tens of sons on several tens of horses and went out the gate; the armies pursued and seized and sent him.
idiomatic: When he knew all was lost he took Li and several sons on several tens of horses out the gate; the armies pursued, seized him, and sent him on.

literal: An edict summoned him to the capital and admonished him with familial teaching.
idiomatic: An edict summoned him to the capital and admonished him with familial teaching.

literal: Whenever Yu stopped at a post station he always took Li by the hand and exhausted private feeling.
idiomatic: Whenever he stopped at a post station he took Li by the hand and gave himself to private feeling.

literal: Though in chains he drank and feasted as before, with hardly a look of shame or fear.
idiomatic: Though in chains he drank and feasted as before, with hardly a look of shame or fear.

literal: At Yewang Yu said to others: "Though the ruler is deeply merciful and cannot bear to kill me, how can I face the August One!"
idiomatic: At Yewang Yu told others, "Though the ruler is deeply merciful and cannot bear to kill me, how can I face the Son of Heaven!"

literal: Thereupon he sobbed, wept, and stopped breathing; he died at twenty-one.
idiomatic: Thereupon he sobbed, wept, and stopped breathing; he died at twenty-one.

literal: Some say Gao Zhao had a man kill him.
idiomatic: Some say Gao Zhao had a man kill him.

literal: He was encoffined in a small coffin and buried.
idiomatic: He was buried in a small coffin.

literal: The sons reached Luoyang and were all pardoned.
idiomatic: His sons reached Luoyang and were all pardoned.

literal: Later Empress Dowager Ling ordered Yu's four sons all attached to the register and posthumously enfeoffed Yu Prince of Lintao.
idiomatic: Later Empress Dowager Ling had Yu's four sons attached to the register and posthumously enfeoffed Yu as Prince of Lintao.

literal: Baoyue then reburied his parents and observed mourning for three years.
idiomatic: Baoyue then reburied his parents and observed three years of mourning.

literal: Prince of Qinghe Yi, styled Xuanren, in youth was clever and wise, handsome of bearing; Xiaowen loved him.
idiomatic: Prince of Qinghe Yi, styled Xuanren, was clever and wise in youth, handsome of bearing; Xiaowen loved him.

literal: Prince of Pengcheng Xie greatly prized and marked him apart, and together said: "This boy's spirit is outwardly grand, inwardly rich at the core; if Heaven grants years, he will continue the Two Souths."
idiomatic: Prince of Pengcheng Xie prized him greatly and said with others, "This boy's spirit is grand without and rich within; if Heaven grants him years, he will continue the Two Souths."

literal: He broadly traversed the classics and histories and comprehensively joined many schools; he had literary talent and was skilled in discourse on principle.
idiomatic: He ranged broadly through the classics and histories, took in many schools, had literary talent, and was skilled in discourse on principle.
